titre_chapitre: Demand Forecasting - Seasonal Trends, Methods, and Forecast Errors

questions.enonce: How is demand decomposed in the general case of a seasonal demand with a trend?
questions.explication: In the general case of seasonal demand with a trend, demand is expressed as the product of the trend factor (T) and the seasonal factor (S), written as D = T times S[span_0](start_span)[span_0](end_span).

questions.enonce: What does the average forecast error (E) primarily allow you to assess in a forecasting model?
options: The centering of the model, since positive and negative errors can compensate each other
The absolute total magnitude of all errors combined
The exact seasonal factor S for future periods
questions.explication: The average forecast error allows you to assess the centering of the model because positive and negative errors can compensate for each other[span_1](start_span)[span_1](end_span).

questions.enonce: When is the moving average method typically used, and what is its limitation?
options: It is used when there is a very small history of sales (such as a startup), but it smooths results quickly and should not be used over a large time horizon[span_2](start_span)[span_2](end_span).
It is used exclusively for long-term strategic planning over 3 years.
It requires at least 50 years of seasonal sales data.
It replaces linear regression entirely for growing trends.
questions.explication: The moving average is used when you only have a very small sales history (like a startup), but it smooths results quickly and making large time horizons with it makes no sense[span_3](start_span)[span_3](end_span).

questions.enonce: What does the Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD) measure when evaluating forecasting performance?
options: The global extent and amount of errors made, considering both positive and negative values in absolute terms[span_4](start_span)[span_4](end_span)
The slope of the linear trend line
questions.explication: Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD) uses absolute values to study the performance of the model and the overall magnitude of errors made, both positive and negative[span_5](start_span)[span_5](end_span).
